messages.subject: Re: about MaAsLin
messages.body_plain:
Hi Alexandre,

Thanks for reaching out. Just wanted to add here that we are currently finishing up development of MaAsLin2 and looking at a possibility of adding phyloseq compatibility for the users. We will email the MaAsLin Google group once we have the release ready (hopefully very soon). In the meantime, please free to let me or Lauren know if you have any questions.

Many thanks,
Himel

> Hi Alexandre - thanks for getting in touch; right now, there's no way to use a phyloseq object directly with MaAsLin1, and the best bet will be to convert through a tabular file like you described. We're close to finishing up MaAsLin2, though, and have discussed providing a native interface like you suggest - Himel Mallick and Lauren McIver, the two main researchers on MaAsLin2, are included on the MaAsLin users list (CCed) and will be able to provide more information.

And also since the last time I used MaAsLin in my own VM is a month ago, I have installed other packages in between this month and now when I try to run MaAsLin again, I got quite a few error message as below, do you have any idea on why is this happening and how can I solve it?

messages.subject: Variable Type
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have a question regarding the interpretation of variable types by Maaslin. I read online that "the clinical metadata can be of any type continuous (for example age and weight), boolean (sex, stool/biopsy), or discrete/factor (cohort groupings and phenotypes). Does this mean Maaslin is unable to find associations with categorical variables?

For example, if I have a metadata variable X where
1 = 1-10 years old
2 = 11-20 years old
3 = 21-30 years old
4 = 31+ years old

Would Maaslin treat variable X as an ordinal continuous type variable? If not, how would Maaslin generate associations with metadata variable X and the species abundance data?

Thank you,
Alina Husain

messages.subject_clean: Random Effects and R versus Galaxy
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

Thanks for providing Maaslin.

I am currently using it to run a mixed model, however I am unsure if I am doing this correctly! The linear model I am wanting to run is lm(OTU~Condition + Storage_Time_months +(1|Pool)

Basically I am a bit worried by the high number of significance values I am getting. And also differences when running a non-mixed model in R versus galaxy versions of masslin.

1. Mixed model

Below is the code that I have run for a mixed model:

Maaslin('Cond_biom_map_fil_100418_maaslin_transp.tsv','maaslin_output_check_4’, dSignificanceLevel = 0.05, dMinAbd = 0.0001, dMinSamp = 0.01, iLastMetadata = 4, strRandomCovariates = ‘Pool’)

I have attached my tsv file. I couldn't get this to work with a config file. Does this code look appropriate? I have attached the run parameters which indicates 'Pool' is being seen as a random covariate.

2. R versus galaxy
Also I tried running the model with no random effects, and received slightly different results between running this in R to running in Galaxy using the below code in R:

 Maaslin('Cond_biom_map_fil_100418_maaslin_transp.tsv','maaslin_output_check_3’, dSignificanceLevel = 0.05, dMinAbd = 0.0001, dMinSamp = 0.01, iLastMetadata = 4)

Attached are the condition sig. results for R and galaxy.

Thanks to anyone who can help
Christina
